main:
How to Get the Perfect Poop: From Switching Dog Food to the 10% Treat Rule

Healthy, firm dog poop comes from the basics, not a secret trick. Feed the same amount at set times; when you change food, don't switch overnight but mix it into the old food little by little over 7 to 10 days; give plenty of water and walks; and keep treats under 10% of daily calories. That's the core of it.

What is "the perfect poop"?

In Korea, dog owners call ideal stool "golden poop": chocolate brown, moist, but firm enough to hold its shape when you pick it up. In this guide we call it the perfect poop. For the full picture, see the dog poop color and texture chart.

1. Set mealtimes, set amounts

When mealtimes are regular, the gut's rhythm becomes regular too, and potty times get easier to predict. Splitting food into meals, such as 2 a day (3 to 4 for puppies), often helps with poop more than free-feeding. Start from the amount recommended on the food bag and adjust as you watch your dog's weight. Overeating makes poop softer and bigger.

2. Switch dog food gradually over 7 to 10 days

Changing food overnight easily leads to diarrhea. The commonly recommended method is to raise the share of new food a little at a time, like this.

DaysOld foodNew food
Days 1–275%25%
Days 3–450%50%
Days 5–625%75%
Day 7 onward0%100%

For dogs with sensitive stomachs, it's fine to add a day to each step and take more than 10 days. If poop turns soft partway through, go back one step.

3. Water and walks

  • Make sure clean water is available at all times. Too little water makes poop hard.
  • The gut moves while your dog walks. Regular walks make for regular poops.
  • Make sure an outdoor-only dog gets enough chances to go. See Why outdoor-only dogs shouldn't hold it.

4. Keep treats under 10% of daily calories

This is the well-known "10% rule." Too many treats throw off nutritional balance and tend to make poop soft. Human food, especially fatty food, can cause diarrhea and pancreatitis, so it's best avoided. Introduce new treats one at a time, starting small.

5. Probiotics and fiber as extras

Dog probiotics and fiber are known to possibly help gut health. But not every dog needs them, and they're an extra to add once the basics (food, water, walks) are steady. If your dog has a health condition or takes medication, check with your vet first.

6. A log shows you the cause

When poop suddenly turns soft or hard, a log lets you find what changed a few days earlier. A new treat, a food switch, or a change in walks are common causes. If soft poop keeps coming, see Why dogs get diarrhea; if hard poop keeps coming, see Dog constipation causes.

This guide is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems tired or unwell, or you're worried about any symptom, talk to your vet.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many days should it take to switch dog food?

The common advice is to raise the share of new food step by step to 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% over 7 to 10 days. If your dog has a sensitive stomach, going even slower is fine.

How many treats can I give my dog?

A commonly cited guideline is to keep treats under 10% of your dog's daily calories. Cut back the regular food a little to make up for treats.

Will probiotics give my dog perfect poop?

They're known to possibly help, but not every dog needs them. Food, water and walks come first, and if your dog has a health condition, check with your vet.

My dog's poop suddenly got soft. What should I check first?

First check for a recent food switch, a new treat, human food or stress. If it lasts more than a day, or there's blood or vomiting, see a vet.
